November 24, 2026

Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs.

An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take.

In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets. Redesigned antibodies also retained binding. Specialized models helped supply sequences and select candidates for testing.

The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry, and biological knowledge to reason about protein shapes and interactions with other molecules.

In a preprint titledGPT‑6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models, we show that our GPT‑6 family of models hasintrinsic capabilitiesfor designing new proteins: the models can design new protein structures and sequences without relying on specialized biology models, using only reasoning and general-purpose coding tools.

Proteins do much of the work in living cells. They drive the chemical reactions that sustain life, carry oxygen through the blood, and defend the body against infection. Incorrectly shaped proteins can also cause disease and dysfunction. Proteins are made from chains of chemical building blocks called amino acids. The order, or sequence, of these amino acids helps determine how a protein folds into a three-dimensional shape, which in turn influences what it does.

Scientists often start with a clear idea of what they want a protein to do. They might want it to block a signal that helps cancer cells evade the immune system or to help capture carbon dioxide from the air. The challenge is to work out what three-dimensional structure would enable the protein to do its job and which amino acid sequence would give it that structure. Specialized biology models capable of generating three-dimensional protein structures and sequences have made this work more practical.

Using and coordinating these specialized models requires substantial expertise. Each accepts particular kinds of inputs and constraints, and these models cannot easily accept new kinds of information without changes to their software or additional training. In contrast, a general-purpose model capable of performing the work of multiple specialized models can easily adapt to new instructions and requirements.

Our research illustrates the potential power of pairing natural language with intrinsic protein capabilities. We could guide our models at scales ranging from a single bond between two atoms to the overall shape of a protein. For example, we asked GPT‑6.2 to predict where and how a small molecule would bind to a protein. When we already knew which two atoms formed a bond, we could give the model that information and ask how the rest of the molecule would fit. We could switch between these tasks simply by changing the prompt, without retraining the model. We also asked our models to design small proteins called minibinders and marked where each should attach to its target, and further specified how many coils or strands each minibinder should contain. An internal model followed that instruction with near-perfect fidelity in its three-dimensional designs.

Points farther from the center indicate better performance. Newer generations of models improved on many of the 14 protein tasks tested.

We ran computational tests of whether the GPT‑6 models series could design small proteins to bind given targets, build proteins around specified structural features, predict protein structures and molecular interactions, and rank how sequence changes affect properties such as stability and binding. Our latest models performed comparably to or better than specialized models on most tasks, although predicting a complete protein structure remained a clear weakness.

The models’ written reasoning and code offer clues to how they approach these tasks. They draw on mathematics, physics, chemistry, and coding alongside knowledge of recurring patterns in protein sequences and structures. For example, when designing a small protein intended to bind to IL-7Rα, the model proposed how the two proteins might interact, then wrote and executed code to explore different protein shapes and amino acid choices that could support that interaction.

The model’s written reasoning and code show it drawing on math, physics, chemistry and biology to design a protein intended to attach to IL-7Rα. It examines the target’s surface, arranges five coiled sections into a protein shape, and checks how the two proteins could fit together.

With our research partner,Onava⁠(opens in a new window), we also tested the models’ structure and sequence designs in the lab. First, Onava made small proteins based on three-dimensional structures designed by a pre-released version of GPT‑6.2. Specialized models supplied amino acid sequences and helped select candidates for testing. For each of the five targets we chose, at least one protein showed evidence of binding in the lab. In separate experiments, GPT‑6.2 designed new amino acid sequences for existing minibinders and antibodies. Following candidate selection with specialized models, many of the redesigned proteins also showed evidence of binding to the same targets as the originals.

Our first laboratory experiment tested whether GPT‑6.2 could design small proteins that would bind to their intended targets. We compared computational measurements of quality against RFdiffusion, a specialized model for protein design, and found that GPT‑6.2’s three-dimensional designs scored slightly lower while our latest internal models scored higher. For the lab experiment, we made proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs and measured how strongly they bound to their targets.

We gave GPT‑6.2 the three-dimensional structures of five target proteins and marked where we wanted a minibinder to attach. It then wrote code to create three-dimensional designs for potential minibinders, without using specialized protein AI models.

To turn GPT‑6.2’s three-dimensional designs into proteins we could test in the lab, we needed amino acid sequences that would fold into the proposed structures. We used a specialized AI model called SolubleMPNN to suggest sequences for each design. Other specialized protein models helped us select candidates predicted to fold as designed and bind at the intended site on the target.

GPT‑6.2 designed shapes for small proteins intended to attach to chosen targets. Specialized models then proposed amino acid sequences—the order of the proteins’ chemical building blocks—and helped select designs for our research partner Onava to make and test in the lab.

We tested 322 minibinders against 5 targets in the lab. Of those, 35 (10.9%) tested positive for binding to their intended target. We found 5 hits for PD-L1 (a protein some cancers use to evade the immune system), 3 for IL-7Rα, 1 for TrkA, 8 for VEGF-A and 18 for IL-17A. Theoriginal RFdiffusion study⁠(opens in a new window)reported higher hit rates, but rates depend heavily on how strictly researchers filter designs before lab validation and their definition of binding. Nevertheless, our results provide early evidence that we can turn GPT‑6.2’s three-dimensional designs into proteins that bind to their intended targets in the lab.

An internal research model designed shapes for small proteins intended to attach to the target proteins shown in gray. The colored shapes compare each design with a computational prediction of how the protein would fold and fit against its target.

We tested whether GPT‑6.2 could design the sequences itself. We gave it three-dimensional models of how existing minibinders fit against their targets, withheld the original amino acid sequences, and asked it to propose new ones. Specialized models helped us choose which proteins to make and test in the lab.

For three targets, we started with computationally predicted structures of confirmed minibinders whose sequences Onava had collected from earlier studies. In our initial lab screens, we saw binding in 75 of 88 designs for MDM2 (85%), 26 of 42 for VEGF-A (62%), and 8 of 59 for PD-1 (14%). The amino acid sequences proposed by GPT‑6.2 also often differed significantly from the original minibinder sequences, with a median of 50% for VEGF-A, 43% for MDM2, and 15% for PD-1.

We also asked GPT‑6.2 to design new sequences for three unpublished minibinder shapes it had generated earlier: two targeting PD-L1 and one targeting IL-7Rα. A specialized model, ProteinMPNN, had already supplied one sequence for each shape, and proteins made from those sequences had shown binding in the lab. Of the 107 proteins made from GPT‑6.2’s new sequences, 14 (13.1%) showed binding.

Given an unpublished structure, GPT‑6.2 had come up with two substantially different sequences that both showed signs of binding to the same target. For the same PD-L1 minibinder structure, GPT‑6.2 designed two sequences different from the original in 52 and 58 out of 90 total amino acids. The two also differed from each other at 44 positions, nearly half the sequence.

The unpublished structures and substantial differences in sequence give us strong evidence that GPT‑6.2’s capabilities extend beyond memorization. The results also suggest we could use GPT‑6.2 to intrinsically design both a minibinder’s structure and its sequence.

Researchers often redesign an antibody’s binding loops to help it grip its target more tightly, a process calledaffinity maturation. They may also want it to bind more selectively, so it’s less likely to attach to similar proteins. articles.title: OpenAI and Cisco Releases Shirudo: An Open-Source Linux Runtime Allowing Agents to Defend Systems Without Downtime
articles.content:
OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime for defending live systems. Shirudo is an eBPF runtime that lets AI agents write temporary “shields” against known exploits. Shields block the vulnerable behavior while legitimate requests keep flowing. Teams get time to test and ship the real patch. The engineering came from Isovalent at Cisco, the team behind Cilium and Tetragon. TL;DR Size: Software runtime, not a model. Code is pre-release. Runs on: Linux on x86-64, arm64 and riscv64, with TPM 2.0 and a patched bpf-next kernel. The quickstart VM example uses 4 CPUs and 4G RAM. Performance: No overhead or latency numbers published. One controlled exploit test is disclosed. Best: A Codex-generated shield blocked Java4Shell (CVSS 9.2) on running Elasticsearch 9.5.5, with no restart. Worst: Targets need a bpf-next kernel plus 5 carried patches not yet in bpf-next. No TPM-less mode. Bottom line: Best: signed, TPM-attested mitigations agents can write in code. What problem does Shirudo solve? Patching takes time. OpenAI team notes that testing and deploying a fix can take days or weeks. Blocking a whole Linux operation is risky, because exploits and normal requests often share it. Shirudo targets that patch window. How does Shirudo work? Shirudo uses eBPF, which runs small verified programs at hooks inside the Linux kernel. The name is Japanese for “shield.” Isovalent calls it a rewrite of Tetragon, its 2022 eBPF security platform. The design splits work across 2 roles: Operator machine: a one-shot CLI, not a daemon. It builds and signs shields, then pushes them to an OCI registry. Signing code never reaches a target. Target node: no persistent Shirudo daemon. Its control plane is an eBPF program loaded at boot. It pulls packages and verifies signatures before loading them. A shield can do 3 things. It can block the code path a bug needs, replace vulnerable code, or add detection visibility. The docs call these packages upatches: small BPF C programs shipped as signed artifacts. There is deliberately no policy DSL. The Linux Plumbers talk by Daniel Borkmann and John Fastabend says agents work better with code directly. What does the agent loop look like? Isovalent describes 4 stages, with Codex as the control plane: Discovery: find bugs or ingest external disclosures. Mitigation: build an exploit reproducer, pick a hook, and iterate until the shield works. Rollout: push signed shields, monitored against a security score and app health. Monitoring: a hit count tracks exploitation attempts against shielded bugs. Operators approve shields before enforcement. Teams can also observe a shield’s impact before it blocks anything. How is trust enforced? The kernel checks each loader’s signature against a .bpf keyring. The eBPF verifier then checks program safety. A TPM 2.0 records every load and unload, and signs attestation evidence. The test bundle uses an ML-DSA-87 signing key, a post-quantum algorithm. Registry traffic uses TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange. articles.summary: 보도에 따르면 OpenAI와 Cisco는 AI 에이전트가 실행 중인 리눅스 시스템에 임시 방어 코드를 적용하도록 지원하는 오픈소스 eBPF 런타임 Shirudo를 공개했다. 정식 패치 배포 전 취약한 동작을 차단하는 방식으로, 통제된 실험에서는 Codex가 생성한 방어 코드가 Elasticsearch의 Java4Shell 공격을 재시작 없이 막았다. 서명과 TPM 기반 검증을 사용하지만 사전 공개 단계이며, 추가 패치가 적용된 커널과 TPM 2.0이 필요하다. 성능 오버헤드 수치와 광범위한 운영 검증은 제공되지 않아 즉시 범용 배포하기보다는 제한된 환경에서 검토할 기술이다.

articles.title: ByteDance Researchers Open-Sources Laminar, an Async Reinforcement Learning RL Post-Training Framework
articles.content: Researchers from The University of Hong Kong and ByteDance Seed have open-sourced Laminar. Laminar is an reinforcement learning RL post-training framework for LLMs and long-horizon agents. The core idea is simple: stop forcing every trajectory and every GPU to wait for the slowest one. For teams training coding agents with long, skewed rollouts, that is where most GPU time goes. TL;DR What: A framework. Tested on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (30.5B total, 3.3B active) and Qwen2.5 at 7B, 32B and 72B. Runs on: Multi-node NVIDIA GPU clusters with Ray and CUDA. Tested on 64x H800 and up to 1024 H800 GPUs. vLLM for inference, Megatron-LM or FSDP2 for training. Performance: Strong end-to-end gains on SWE agent RL and up to 5.48x throughput in the paper. Best: 52.2% on SWE-bench Verified, up from 46.6% for the base model. Worst: Early repo (1 commit at launch), vLLM is the only listed inference backend, and per-step async checkpointing is still in progress. Bottom line: Best: fewer samples and GPU-hours to a higher SWE-bench score. Worst: the headline comparison mixes H800 and H100 hardware. What is Laminar? Laminar is an asynchronous RL post-training framework that decouples rollout, buffering, training and weight transfer into independent loops. It is built on verl and Uni-Agent and released under Apache-2.0. The launch blog splits the stack into 3 layers. verl provides training and inference compute backends. Uni-Agent handles agent execution, tool calls and sandboxes. Laminar handles cluster-scale orchestration. How does Laminar’s architecture work? The design rests on 3 principles: full decoupling, fine-grained asynchrony and fault tolerance. Rollout loop: Drives agent interactions and serves generation across inference replicas. Experience buffer (data plane): Separates trajectory production from training and serves ready batches on demand. Training loop: Samples batches, computes advantages and off-policy corrections, and publishes weights. Weight Relay (weight plane): The trainer stages weights into per-node shared CPU memory and keeps going. Replicas pull updates on their own schedule. In the research paper, relays are CPU processes, 1 per rollout machine. They broadcast weights along a pipelined RDMA chain. A 72B model reaches 127 other relays in under 1.6 seconds. What is version-consistent rollout? Most async systems use version-mixed partial rollout. They interrupt in-flight trajectories at each weight update and resume under the new policy. That forces repeated re-prefill. Laminar also supports a version-consistent mode. Each trajectory finishes under 1 policy version. Replicas update independently, without a global weight-switch barrier. The blog states that this keeps the prefix KV cache intact. It argues re-prefill cost scales cubically with sequence length under frequent updates. Repack handles the tail. Once new weights exist, leftover old-version trajectories are consolidated onto fewer replicas. Drained replicas then load the new version immediately. && How does Laminar perform on SWE-bench Verified? The research team trained Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on SWE-rebench. They evaluated on all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks with greedy decoding. Base model: 46.6% (233/500). Baseline peak (step 150, 64x H100): 51.4% with 76.4k samples and 5,085 GPU-hours. Laminar match (step 320, 64x H800): 51.4% with 41.0k samples (46% fewer) and 1,450 GPU-hours (71% fewer). Laminar peak (step 400, 64x H800): 52.2% with 51.2k samples (33% fewer) and 1,843 GPU-hours (64% fewer). How does Laminar handle failures? Faults stay local. If a rollout replica fails, the router fences only that replica. It restarts, reloads weights from the local relay and resumes from its generated token prefix. A replica that fails during weight loading recovers without blocking the trainer. Trainer checkpoints align model state, prompt cursors and published weight versions. laminar.eval also evaluates several checkpoints at once across resident replicas, in batch or streaming mode during training. It used 33% fewer samples and 64% fewer GPU-hours, on different GPUs than the baseline. The code is Apache-2.0 but early, with vLLM-only inference. articles.title: OmniEvaluator: AI 모델과 에이전트를 위한 통합 평가 프레임워크
articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 발표 내용 AI 서비스를 만들 때 "이 모델, 우리 서비스에 써도 될까?"라는 질문은 도입 전(후보 모델·API·툴 조합 비교)과 도입 후(의도대로 서빙되는지, 패치·버전별 차이) 반복해서 돌아옵니다. 그런데 이 질문에 답하는 비용은 큽니다. 모달리티마다 평가 툴킷이 다르고, 같은 벤치마크라도 프롬프트·파서·메트릭 구현에 따라 점수가 수십 점씩 갈라지며, 결과는 사람 손으로 모아야 합니다. ​ OmniEvaluator는 이 문제를 구조적으로 푸는 통합 평가 프레임워크입니다. 추론 엔진 4종(HF Transformers·vLLM·SGLang·상용 API)과 평가 프레임워크 4종(lm-eval-harness·lmms-eval·VLMEvalKit·built-in)을 하나의 중간 스키마로 연결해 텍스트·이미지·비디오·오디오 1,000개 이상의 벤치마크를 하나의 인터페이스로 실행합니다. 모든 실행은 설정·예측·점수를 담은 아티팩트로 남아 그대로 재현할 수 있고, CPU에서 도는 내장 Verifier가 프롬프트·프레임워크 차이에 흔들리지 않는 채점 신호를 제공합니다. 2026년에는 Agent Harness가 추가되어 기존 벤치마크에 옵션 두 개만 붙이면 툴 호출 궤적까지 채점하는 Agent 평가로 전환되며, 대시보드에서 요청 → 진행 → 결과 → 샘플을 한곳에서 확인할 수 있습니다. ​ 관련 자료 논문: A Composable Evaluation System for Reproducible Omni-Modal Foundation Model Evaluation (EMNLP 2026 System Demonstrations, arXiv 2609.01315) 공개 저장소 : https://github.com/naver-ai/omni-evaluator ​ 발표 대상 AI 서비스 기획자: 서비스 도입 전 후보 모델·API·툴 조합의 구현 가능성과 가치를 정량적으로 비교하려는 분 AI Engineer / Forward Deployment Engineer: 도입 후 모델이 의도대로 서빙되는지, 패치·버전·서빙엔진별 차이를 정량 확인하려는 분 모델 평가 담당자: 여러 모달리티·프레임워크에 걸친 평가 환경을 하나로 통합하려는 분 ​ 목차 평가의 어려움 OmniEvaluator 구조 Agent Harness 대시보드 — 리더보드, 샘플 뷰어, Trigger Claude Plugin 팀 운영 사례 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.
articles.summary: 네이버는 텍스트·이미지·비디오·오디오 모델과 에이전트를 하나의 인터페이스로 평가하는 OmniEvaluator를 소개했다. 네 종류의 추론 엔진과 네 종류의 평가 프레임워크를 공통 중간 스키마로 연결해 1,000개 이상의 벤치마크를 실행하고, 설정·예측·점수를 재현 가능한 아티팩트로 남긴다. CPU 기반 Verifier와 도구 호출 궤적을 채점하는 Agent Harness도 제공해 평가 구현 차이와 에이전트 행동을 함께 점검하도록 설계됐다. 공개 저장소를 제공하는 만큼 모델 선정부터 서빙 엔진 변경 이후의 회귀 평가까지 통합하려는 개발팀에 실용적인 도구다.

articles.title: 운영자의 시간을 아끼는 AI 에이전트 2부 - MCP 부터 Agent 설계까지

articles.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI models vary enormously in capability and price. Model routing exploits this by sending easier tasks to cheaper models. However, a single agentic task often combines easy and difficult subtasks, making one model choice for the entire task inefficient. We introduce partial routing, which guides a frontier lead model to delegate suitable subtasks to a cheaper worker model. From both models' past runs, we identify recurring subtasks and measure each model's quality and cost on them. These measurements produce delegation guidance, with a parameter, $\delta$, controlling how much is delegated. The lead decides when and what to delegate during execution, without training either model. On held-out tasks from ViBench and Terminal-Bench 4.0, partial routing achieves higher mean task performance than the lead alone and task-level routing. With $\delta = 0.75$, it raises the lead's ViBench score from 70.2 to 78.5 at 19% lower cost, and its Terminal-Bench pass rate from 54% to 61% at similar cost. Giving the lead only the subtask breakdown, without a worker, also reduces cost on both benchmarks and raises the Terminal-Bench pass rate. These results show that analysis of past runs can support more efficient planning and more effective delegation, with little cost and implementation overhead.
articles.summary: Partial Routing은 작업 전체를 한 모델에 배정하는 대신, 고성능 주도 모델이 일부 하위 작업을 저렴한 모델에 위임하도록 만드는 방법이다. 두 모델의 과거 실행 기록에서 하위 작업별 품질과 비용을 측정해 위임 지침을 만들며, 별도 모델 학습은 요구하지 않는다. 평가에서는 ViBench 점수를 70.2에서 78.5로 높이면서 비용을 19% 줄였고, Terminal-Bench에서는 비슷한 비용으로 통과율을 54%에서 61%로 높였다. 하위 작업 분해만 제공해도 일부 개선이 나타나, 성과에는 위임 자체뿐 아니라 계획 구조화의 효과도 포함된다.

articles.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. It further separates harm characterization from intervention decisions, thus enabling safety policies to be specified outside the model weights through explicit, clinician-curated instructions that can be updated and audited. We validate the taxonomy with expert clinicians and validate a panel of LLM judges to scale annotation. Relabeling public benchmarks in this taxonomy shows that they rarely contain harm directed at the user, which accounts for nearly half of the harm in real conversations. We then train MindGuard2, a 35B-A3B reasoning-based guard model using supervised fine-tuning on short reasoning traces followed by reinforcement learning with a reasoning-length penalty, to minimize inference overhead while preserving the benefits of reasoning. On two public benchmarks and real-world conversations, MindGuard2 achieves balanced accuracy comparable to the substantially larger GLM-5.3 at approximately 10x lower median latency, advancing the accuracy-latency Pareto frontier. Furthermore, it achieves low false-positive rates at high recall, helping balance the need to detect unsafe situations against the risk of unnecessary interventions that may disrupt support and undermine user trust. We release a safety guardrail model with SOTA performance trained on synthetic data, together with synthetic conversations and annotations of public benchmarks in our taxonomy.
articles.summary: MindGuard2 연구는 정신건강 대화의 위험을 위해의 종류, 관련 주체, 발생 시점으로 나누고 위험 파악과 개입 결정을 분리했다. 임상의가 작성한 외부 정책으로 개입 기준을 수정·감사할 수 있게 하며, 짧은 추론 학습과 추론 길이 페널티를 사용한 강화학습으로 지연을 줄였다. 연구진은 35B-A3B 모델이 공개 벤치마크와 실제 대화 평가에서 더 큰 GLM-5.3과 유사한 균형 정확도를 약 10배 낮은 중앙 지연시간으로 달성했다고 보고했다. 정신건강 지원 서비스의 안전장치에 유용한 접근이지만, 분류 성능이 임상적 효과나 모든 위험 상황의 탐지를 보장하지는 않는다.

articles.title: Meet Facebook’s Your Algorithm: How Meta Turns Plain-Language Preferences Into Ranking
articles.content: Meta has published an engineering deep dive on Facebook Your Algorithm. Your Algorithm lets people tell Facebook, in plain language, what they want in Feed and Reels. Meta announced the feature on October 13, 2026. The new post shows how large language models (LLMs) sit inside a production recommender. For developers, it is a rare look at explicit preferences wired into an implicit-signal ranking stack. TL;DR What: ‘Your algorithm is an end-to-end system that addresses the limitations of adaptability and nuance in recommendations’ Runs on: Meta’s server-side ranking stack, plus on-device cache invalidation in the Facebook app. Best: Explicit interests feed 4 retrieval sources and apply across both Feed and Reels. Bottom line: Best: a clear blueprint for LLM-steered ranking What is Facebook Your Algorithm? Your Algorithm is an AI-powered preference page for Facebook Feed and Reels. It has 3 parts, per Meta’s engineering post. A one-sentence “Lately Summary” describes recent viewing. An “Interested In” list is prefilled from past activity. A “Not Interested In” list holds exclusions. Users can type interests, move them between lists, or delete them. Access is through the three-dot menu on posts, according to Meta’s newsroom. Meta’s framing is simple. Implicit engagement signals scale well but adapt slowly and miss nuance. Explicit, stated preferences close that gap. How does the Your Algorithm system work? Meta splits the preference lifecycle into 4 components: Profile generation: An LLM turns regularly refreshed interest signals into readable topic names. It also writes the Lately Summary. Preference management: An LLM checks that a typed phrase is a coherent topic. It detects duplicates and maps the phrase to a clean topic name. This step runs on a smaller, cheaper model. Ranking: Both lists are applied across the ranking funnel. Delivery optimization: Changes reach the feed faster. Validated interests are enriched with an embedding and search keywords. They are saved to a shared store that both Feed and Reels read. A separate component runs integrity and safety checks. How do “Interested In” topics reach the feed? Each interest drives 4 retrieval sources. 2 match content directly: search and clusters of closely related topics. 2 extend reach: the content graph and item-to-item similarity. A relevance check compares the interest’s meaning with each candidate. Passing candidates get a late-stage ranking promotion. A reranking control layer then stops flooding: Repeats of the same interest are spaced out. Each interest’s daily contribution is capped. Retrieval fetches for 1 interest per request. New interests get temporary extra weight. How does “Not Interested In” filtering work? Meta calls this layered filtering at every stage. Ranking uses embedding comparison to remove close matches. Demotion rules push down near matches. A fine-tuned LLM reranker then reviews the final list. Quality requests, such as less AI-generated or sexually suggestive content, take a different path. They map to dedicated demotion signals, not topic matching. Requests naming a creator filter that creator directly. On the client, cache invalidation removes queued items that match a new exclusion before display. Why use a small fine-tuned LLM as the reranker? The reranker is trained to return only the items to remove. Meta says this small fine-tuned model beat a general-purpose model judging each item. It was faster and more reliable. Outputting a short removal list is cheaper than scoring every candidate. Speed comes from a “supplementary tail load.” Adding an interest fires an extra fetch outside the normal cycle. Meta gives no latency figure for it. articles.title: 사이냅소프트, 엑셀·한글 문서 원본 구조 그대로 AI 데이터로…GPU 없이 초당 154.8페이지 처리
articles.content:
문서 인공지능(Document AI) 전문기업 사이냅소프트(대표 전경헌)는 문서 파서 솔루션 ‘사이냅 도큐애널라이저(Synap Document Analyzer)’를 도입한 고객들이 엑셀과 한글 문서의 원본 구조를 보존하는 데이터 추출 정확도를 주요 선택 이유로 꼽았다고 26일 밝혔다.

사이냅 도큐애널라이저는 엑셀 시트에 흩어진 표 영역을 자동으로 인식하고 행·열 구조와 병합 셀의 머리글 및 하위 데이터 간 관계를 유지한다. HWP·HWPX 문서도 PDF 변환 없이 문단, 표, 다단 정보와 읽기 순서까지 구조화한다.

추출한 데이터는 마크다운(Markdown)과 JSON 등으로 제공해 거대언어모델(LLM) 및 검색증강생성(RAG) 시스템 구축에 활용할 수 있다. 특히 GPU 없이 CPU만으로 초당 154.8페이지(동시 사용자 16명 기준)를 처리한다. 한국수력원자력, 한국주택금융공사, 삼성디스플레이, 현대건설, 토스랩 등이 도입해 활용하고 있다.

전경헌 사이냅소프트 대표는 “엑셀과 한글 문서를 원본 구조 그대로 읽어내는 문서 기술이 고객의 선택으로 이어지고 있는 만큼, 공공과 기업의 문서를 AI가 바로 쓰는 데이터로 만드는 데 집중하겠다”고 말했다.

한편, 사이냅 도큐애널라이저는 65억5000만원 규모의 법제처 ‘생성형 AI 법령검색 시스템 구축’ 사업에서 법령 원천 데이터의 구조 분석과 JSON 데이터셋 구축을 담당하고 있으며, 지난 4월 GS인증 1등급을 획득했다.
articles.summary: 사이냅소프트는 도큐애널라이저가 엑셀 표의 행·열 및 병합 셀 관계와 HWP·HWPX의 문단·표·읽기 순서를 보존해 데이터를 추출한다고 밝혔다. 한글 문서를 PDF로 변환하지 않고 처리하며, 결과를 마크다운과 JSON으로 제공해 LLM 및 RAG 구축에 연결한다. 회사는 동시 사용자 16명 조건에서 GPU 없이 CPU만으로 초당 154.8페이지를 처리한다고 설명했고, 공공기관과 기업의 도입 사례도 제시했다. 국내 업무 문서의 구조 손실을 줄이는 실용성이 있지만, 처리량은 제시된 조건의 회사 발표 수치로 보아야 한다.

articles.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
articles.content: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.
articles.summary: 미국 주 법무장관들이 Character.AI의 파산 매각안에 포함된 이용자 개인 대화 데이터 처분 계획에 이의를 제기했다고 보도됐다. 이들은 매각 대상에 미국 계정 2,100만 개 이상의 민감한 개인정보가 포함되며, 그중 210만 개는 미성년자 등록 계정이라고 밝혔다. 대화형 AI의 사업 재편 과정에서도 축적된 대화 데이터의 보호와 이전 조건이 핵심 쟁점이 된 사례이며, 제공 자료만으로 매각 승인 여부나 최종 데이터 처리 방침은 확인할 수 없다.

articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
articles.content: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
articles.summary: 보도에 따르면 뉴욕은 AI 챗봇 장난감을 5년간 금지했다. 기사에는 Common Sense Media 연구가 부적절한 콘텐츠 노출과 정서 발달 위험을 포함한 안전 문제를 제기했다고 소개돼 있다. 아동 대상 대화형 AI의 제품 설계와 시장 진입에 직접 영향을 줄 수 있는 조치지만, 제공된 자료에는 구체적인 적용 범위나 예외 및 시행 조건이 없어 세부 규제 요건까지 판단하기는 어렵다.

articles.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). Instead of the conventional low-rank product, the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling: because rank is multiplicative under this product, $A$ multiplies the rank of $M(x)$ by $p$ without adding trainable parameters. The factor $M(x)$ is further decomposed as $B_1\,\mathrm{diag}(g(x))\,B_2$, where the input gate $g(x)$, computed once per sample by a network shared across all adapted layers, adjusts the rank of the update to each input in steps of $p$. Where input conditioning is unnecessary, the gate is folded into $B_1$ at deployment. Because the gate changes the rank only in discrete steps, the benefit of input conditioning can be predicted before training from a few hundred labeled inputs. Across six medical imaging and language benchmarks, KiRA attains the highest mean score against five published baselines with 8.7--9.7 times fewer trainable parameters than low-rank adaptation, and the pre-training criterion agrees with the measured benefit of input conditioning on all six tasks.
articles.summary: KiRA는 고정된 무작위 행렬과 학습 가능한 인자의 크로네커 곱을 사용해 저랭크 미세조정의 표현력 제약을 완화하는 방법이다. 입력별 게이트가 업데이트의 랭크를 조절하며, 입력 조건화가 필요하지 않은 경우에는 배포 시 게이트를 가중치 인자에 통합한다. 의료 영상과 언어 분야의 6개 벤치마크에서 LoRA보다 학습 파라미터가 8.7~9.7배 적으면서 비교 대상 5개 방법 중 가장 높은 평균 점수를 기록했다고 보고했다. 적은 학습 자원으로 모델을 적응시키는 가능성을 제시하지만, 결과의 범위는 평가된 과제에 한정된다.

articles.title: Fast and Scalable Abstract Interpretation for Deep Neural Networks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33259v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Abstract interpretation can certify properties of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), but precise analyses remain expensive. General implementations repeat work when analyzing the same architecture under different inputs and properties. Interleaving this work with numerical operations limits GPU utilization and restricts how much of the analysis a tensor compiler can process together.
  We present Scepter, a framework for specializing DNN abstract interpreters through structural semantics. The semantics determine the structure of intermediate abstract values while deferring their numerical evaluation. Structural computations from successive operations can therefore be performed together before certification, generating an executable tensor program. With the abstract interpreter and DNN architecture fixed, the program can be reused with different weights and input regions. We prove that it computes the same bounds as the general interpreter in exact arithmetic. The generated program also exposes operations and their dependencies for tensor compilation and memory planning. We implement Scepter for the tensor programs that Neuton generates from ConstraintFlow specifications.
  We evaluate Scepter on eight abstract interpreters and 44 DNNs against six baseline systems on GPUs and CPUs. Scepter handles networks with up to 153x as many neurons as the largest completed by the corresponding baselines. It completes DeepPoly on ResNet50 and VGG-16, whereas none of the evaluated DeepPoly baselines completes either network. On configurations completed by both systems, GPU geometric-mean speedups over Neuton range from 11.9x to 44.4x across eight analyses, with a 2.60x geometric-mean reduction in peak memory. In an input-splitting case study, Scepter proves 68 properties for which the baselines time out.
  Code: https://github.com/uiuc-focal-lab/constraintflow.git
articles.summary: Scepter는 신경망의 속성을 인증하는 추상 해석에서 구조 계산과 수치 계산을 분리해 재사용 가능한 텐서 프로그램을 생성한다. 같은 모델 구조에 대해 입력 영역이나 가중치가 바뀌어도 프로그램을 재사용할 수 있으며, 정확한 산술에서는 기존 해석기와 같은 경계를 계산함을 증명했다. 8개 추상 해석기와 44개 신경망 평가에서 Neuton 대비 GPU 기하평균 속도 향상은 분석별 11.9~44.4배였고, 피크 메모리는 기하평균 기준 2.60배 줄었다. 기존 비교 시스템이 완료하지 못한 ResNet50과 VGG-16의 DeepPoly 분석도 수행해 대형 모델 검증의 적용 범위를 넓혔다.

articles.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33513v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents that operate in the real world must reason correctly and on-time, yet they currently do not account for how time should alter their reasoning. Modern agents learn to do tasks in environments that are entirely synchronous: where the world waits for the agent to act before changing. A real-time environment, by contrast, changes independent of the agent. Existing approaches try to bridge this gap by imposing a ratio of thinking to acting. However, for an agent to succeed in real-time it must learn to act quickly when delay is costly and to reason longer when the benefit outweighs the missed opportunities. To this end, we introduce real-time reasoning training (RRT) as the class of training techniques for real-time reasoning agents. We develop three standard RRT techniques: (1) using real-time data, (2) decoupling acting and observing, and (3) curriculum learning in time. Together, these simple techniques substantially outperform strong baselines. Across time pressures, we outperform the strongest non-RRT baseline by an average of 33% reward on in-distribution and 55% reward on out-of-distribution tasks in two real-time environments: Frogger and Snake. These results demonstrate that we can teach agents to balance reasoning and responsiveness under real-time constraints, and that RRT opens a broad, new set of capabilities for real-time agents.
articles.summary: 실시간 추론 학습 RRT는 환경이 에이전트의 사고를 기다리지 않는 상황에서 추론 시간과 행동 시점을 함께 학습하는 접근이다. 실시간 데이터 사용, 관찰과 행동의 분리, 시간 압박에 대한 커리큘럼을 결합해 지연 비용에 따라 사고량을 조절한다. Frogger와 Snake의 두 환경에서는 가장 강한 비RRT 기준선보다 평균 보상이 분포 내 과제에서 33%, 분포 밖 과제에서 55% 높았다고 보고했다. 실시간 에이전트 설계에 시사점이 있지만, 게임에서의 개선을 실제 로봇이나 운영 시스템의 성능으로 바로 일반화할 수는 없다.

articles.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
articles.content: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps. Thus, we propose CAPER (Capacity-Aware Part-grounding and Evidence Refinement), a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that enables VLMs to generate assembly procedures with two modules--PartGround and PlanRefine. PartGround aligns step-level manual evidence with product-specific inventory and part-reference information to identify exact Part IDs and quantities, transforming free-form hardware prediction into evidence-guided assignments represented in a shared Assembly Intermediate Representation (Assembly IR). PlanRefine audits PartGround assignments against finite inventory by removing the lowest-confidence assignments. Uncertain identity cases remain marked for review in the Assembly IR. We evaluate CAPER on the IKEA Assembly in the Wild (IAW) dataset. Experiment results show that CAPER reaches a Finite-inventory Consistency Rate of 83.33% and produces zero observed out-of-inventory Part-ID occurrences. At the plan level, PlanRefine removes all observed inventory-overuse pairs (9 -> 0) and excess units (51 -> 0). Overall, the results indicate that PartGround and PlanRefine improve part reliability, while also enhancing finite-inventory consistency and local prediction accuracy. Project page and video: https://xhzzzz123.github.io/CAPER/
articles.summary: CAPER는 조립 설명서를 읽는 비전언어모델이 부품을 혼동하거나 존재하지 않는 부품 ID를 생성하는 문제를 줄이는 로봇 조립 계획 프레임워크다. PartGround가 설명서 근거와 제품별 부품 목록을 연결하고, PlanRefine이 유한한 재고와 대조해 신뢰도가 낮은 할당을 제거하며 불확실한 항목은 검토 대상으로 남긴다. IKEA Assembly in the Wild 평가에서는 재고 일관성 비율 83.33%를 기록했고, 관측된 재고 외 부품 ID와 재고 초과 사용을 제거했다. 이는 계획의 신뢰성 개선 결과이며, 실제 로봇의 조립 성공률이 입증됐다는 뜻은 아니다.

articles.title: EditText: Structure-Aware Generation and Selective Visual Transport for Fine-Grained Text Editing
articles.content: Fine-grained text editing aims to accurately replace text in a specified region while preserving the source text's font, color, and texture, as well as visual consistency in unedited regions. We present EditText, a unified framework for fine-grained text editing that combines target character generation with visual transport from the source image. The model uses dual-condition Fill inputs: a masked image and a source text style reference, both sharing a spatial reference with the target image. The masked image hides the original text and retains unedited content as a source canvas; the style reference supplies appearance cues that guide new character generation together with the target text. We introduce an Attention Transport framework in which Source Weight describes the attention allocated to a condition and the Spatial Aggregation Kernel describes its internal spatial attention distribution. Accurate transfer of source details depends on attention strength, the retention of details in condition features, and spatially accurate aggregation. For selected non-edit queries, we therefore preserve the total attention weight assigned to the masked image while redistributing its attention toward spatially corresponding neighborhoods, enabling selective visual transport. Multi-stage training, combined with a Glyph-aware Structural Loss on local target character structure, teaches the model to generate accurate text, preserve source text appearance, and retain unedited details. We also introduce TBench, a fine-grained text editing benchmark covering Alphabetic, Logographic, and Arabic numerals, to evaluate character updates, appearance preservation, and the preservation of unedited details. On TBench, EditText achieves state-of-the-art non-edit-region SSIM (0.9769) and full-image LPIPS (0.0460).
articles.summary: EditText는 이미지의 특정 글자만 바꾸면서 원래 글꼴·색상·질감과 편집하지 않은 영역을 보존하는 프레임워크다. 마스킹된 이미지와 원문 스타일 참조를 함께 사용하고, 선택적 어텐션 재분배와 글리프 구조 손실로 문자 생성과 원본 세부 정보 보존을 결합한다. 연구진이 제시한 TBench에서 비편집 영역 SSIM 0.9769와 전체 이미지 LPIPS 0.0460으로 최고 성능을 보고했다. 디자인 수정과 이미지 내 문구 교체에 유용할 수 있지만, 제시된 수치는 해당 벤치마크의 시각적 보존 성능이며 모든 문자 체계의 정확성을 보장하지는 않는다.

articles.title: Typical Angina, Reversed: A Long-Standing Documentation Error in the UCI Heart Disease Data
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The UCI Heart Disease data are a widely used machine-learning benchmark. We show that their chest-pain variable is stored in reverse of its documentation. At all four sites, the code documented as "asymptomatic" (4) marks patients with typical angina, and the code documented as "typical angina" (1) marks patients with almost none of the classical angina features (at Cleveland, no chest pain).
  Two complementary checks establish this: (i) the chest-pain table and regression coefficients of the original 1986 Cleveland study are reproduced only under the corrected reading; (ii) in the Budapest, Switzerland and Long Beach files, 93-96% of patients coded 4 have all three classical angina features. A 1990 word-labeled Cleveland file already uses the documented labels, and Statlog (Heart), a Cleveland subset, stores the same codes. OpenML, PMLB and two highly voted Kaggle copies that name the categories use the same documented labels (about 400,000 downloads combined).
  We audited a seeded random sample of 150 records from a pre-specified Scholar query for SHAP studies of these data mentioning asymptomatic chest pain (124 readable). Of 32 papers that state a direction for a named category, 25 (78%; 95% CI 61-89%) state one inconsistent with the corrected category identities; 22 (69%; 51-82%; post hoc) are attributable to the documentation error, and nine of these explain it clinically. None of the 124 readable papers identifies the reversal.
  Conventional models are essentially unaffected, one reason the error went unnoticed. Interpretations that attach the documented names to model effects are reversed, and zero-shot language-model classifiers that read the labels are misled: with the documented labels, three open-weight models lose 0.12-0.33 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) given age, sex and chest-pain type. We give the corrected mapping, evidence and code.
articles.summary: 연구진은 널리 쓰이는 UCI Heart Disease 데이터에서 흉통 변수의 전형적 협심증과 무증상 범주 코드가 문서 설명과 뒤바뀌어 있다고 보고했다. 원래 연구의 표·회귀계수 재현과 다른 병원 데이터의 임상 특징 대조를 근거로 들었으며, 검토한 논문 중 범주별 효과 방향을 명시한 32편의 25편이 수정된 범주 의미와 맞지 않았다고 밝혔다. 일반적인 예측 모델의 성능은 대체로 유지되지만 범주 이름에 근거한 해석은 뒤집힐 수 있고, 잘못된 라벨을 읽은 3개 언어모델은 AUC가 0.12~0.33 낮아졌다. 의료 AI에서 예측 점수뿐 아니라 데이터 사전과 설명의 정확성을 재검증해야 함을 보여준다.

articles.title: Online Prediction System for Proactive Autoscaling
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33332v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an online learning system for short-term time series forecasting that enables proactive autoscaling in large-scale distributed systems. Unlike traditional forecasting methods that focus on modeling seasonality and long-term trends, the system targets high-accuracy, low-latency predictions for immediate future intervals for dynamic resource management in internet-scale infrastructures. The system employs a two-stage architecture: a seasonality decomposition stage followed by a residual correction stage using lightweight linear models with engineered features. By retraining models on-the-fly for every prediction cycle, the online prediction system continuously adapts to changing demand patterns without requiring persistent model storage or feature drift monitoring. Deployed across many heterogeneous services, the system processes over 900K predictions per hour; in an offline evaluation on production traffic, its STL-based configuration reduces prediction error (MAPE) by 18.6\% relative to the previous production model. In production, the system has saved an estimated 118K servers daily.
articles.summary: 온라인 예측 시스템 연구는 계절성 분해와 경량 선형 모델의 잔차 보정을 결합해 대규모 서비스의 단기 수요를 예측한다. 매 예측 주기마다 다시 학습해 수요 변화에 대응하며, 여러 서비스에서 시간당 90만 건이 넘는 예측을 처리한다고 보고했다. 운영 트래픽을 이용한 오프라인 평가에서 기존 운영 모델 대비 MAPE를 18.6% 줄였고, 실제 운영에서는 매일 약 11만8,000대의 서버를 절감한 것으로 추정했다. 복잡한 대형 모델 없이도 선제적 오토스케일링의 효율을 높일 수 있다는 사례이나 서버 절감량은 연구진의 운영 추정치다.

articles.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33307v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in high-resource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls only half as much: a threshold set for 95\% accuracy in English yields 90% in Tamil. The size of the loss is set by the language and the base model rather than by leaderboard rank. In 81 controlled fine-tuning runs, task skill learned in English transfers to other languages and a few thousand target-language items narrow large losses, but neither more data nor full-parameter tuning closes them. Finally, the same test items are answered more accurately in all 23 benchmark--language pairs we compare when an LLM rather than a person translated them, so LLM-translated test sets understate the gap.
articles.summary: 연구진은 선택지별 확률을 반환하는 공개 가중치 의사결정 모델 25개를 17개 과제와 14개 언어에서 평가했다. 모든 모델은 영어 대비 다른 평가 언어에서 정확도가 낮아졌지만 신뢰도 하락은 그 절반 수준에 그쳤으며, 영어에서 95% 정확도에 맞춘 임계값이 타밀어에서는 90% 정확도를 보였다. 소량의 대상 언어 데이터가 격차를 줄였지만 완전히 해소하지는 못했고, LLM이 번역한 시험 문항은 사람이 번역한 문항보다 성능을 높게 보여 격차를 과소평가했다. 다국어 라우터와 안전장치에는 영어 기준 임계값을 그대로 적용하기보다 언어별 평가와 보정이 필요하다는 결과다.
